title: If they are struggling, give them time. Forgiving it is better.
subtitle: Mercy toward the person who owes you

key.label: What to do with a struggling debtor

then: Before Islam, a lender would say at the deadline: {trap}pay now or the debt grows{/trap}. Abu Qatadah found a man hiding from him over a debt. When the man said he truly had nothing, {reward}Abu Qatadah wept{/reward} and recalled the Prophet ﷺ: whoever gives his debtor time or forgives him {reward}will be in the shade of the Throne{/reward}.
now: Your friend still owes you from last year. He avoids your calls. You could post about it in the group chat. {idea}Or you could ask, are you really struggling?{/idea} And if he is, give him time, or let it go.
old: If someone owes me, I have every right to keep pushing.
new: Giving a struggling person time is charity, and forgiving the debt is even better.
try: Message someone who owes you and tell them to take the time they need.

title: Fear the Day you are returned to Allah and paid in full.
subtitle: Every deal ends in front of Him
then: This verse closes the passage on riba and debts. After {trap}war against those who persist{/trap} and {reward}mercy for the struggling debtor{/reward}, Allah turns every reader to one Day: each soul is returned to Him and paid for what it earned, and {idea}no one is treated unjustly{/idea}.
now: The invoice you padded a little. The deposit you kept from a tenant. The debt you forgave quietly. {idea}All of it reaches the same final desk.{/idea} Nothing is lost, nothing is inflated.
old: Once a deal is done, it is done.
new: Every deal I make will be settled again, fairly, before Allah.
try: Settle one small unfinished money matter today, fairly.

title: The longest verse in the Qur'an asks you to write debts down.
subtitle: Writing it down protects the friendship
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {idea}the longest verse in the Qur'an{/idea}. It came to people in Madinah dealing in loans and advance sales. Writing is {idea}more just, stronger as evidence, and nearer to preventing doubt{/idea}. He says writing for someone who cannot is {reward}a kind of charity{/reward}, as Allah taught the writer.
now: You lend your cousin a few hundred. No note, no date. A year later you each remember it differently and Eid is awkward. {idea}A two-line message with the amount and the date would have saved the relationship.{/idea}
old: Writing down a loan to family shows I do not trust them.
new: Writing it down is an act of justice that protects both of us and our bond.
try: Write down, with the date, any money you currently owe or are owed.

title: If you are trusted, honor it. Do not hide the truth.
subtitle: Trust and testimony when no paper exists

row.title: not my business
sub: I will keep out of it

then: Anas reported that the Prophet ﷺ died with {reward}his shield pledged to a Jewish man of Madinah for barley for his family{/reward}. When people trust each other without paper, the one trusted must return it. Ibn Abbas said hiding true testimony is like false testimony, and the verse says {trap}his heart is sinful{/trap}.
now: Your friend left her laptop with you. Your colleague asked you to hold the petty cash. You saw what really happened in the car park. {idea}The trust is yours to keep, and the truth is yours to tell.{/idea}
old: If nothing is written, I am not really accountable.
new: Trust without paper is still a trust, and Allah knows what I saw.
try: Return one thing you borrowed, or keep one promise you were trusted with, today.

title: Whatever you show or hide in yourself, Allah knows it.
subtitle: The verse that brought the Companions to their knees
then: Abu Hurayrah said when this verse came, {trap}the Companions fell to their knees: we cannot bear this{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ said: do not say we hear and disobey; say {reward}we hear and obey, Your forgiveness, our Lord{/reward}. When they said it, Allah sent the next two verses.
now: Thoughts you are ashamed of. Envy you would never say aloud. Intrusive thoughts at prayer. {idea}You cannot hide them from Allah.{/idea} The Companions felt that weight too, and the answer was to turn toward Him, not away.
old: My inner thoughts are completely private.
new: Allah sees inside me, so I bring all of it to Him and say: we hear and obey.
try: When an ugly thought passes today, say: Ghufranaka Rabbana, Your forgiveness, our Lord.

title: We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord.
subtitle: The answer the Companions gave, now part of the Qur'an
then: The words the Companions spoke in fear became {reward}verses of the Qur'an{/reward}. On the Night Journey the Prophet ﷺ was given {reward}the five prayers and these last verses of Al-Baqarah{/reward}. He said whoever recites the last two verses at night, {idea}they will suffice him{/idea}.
now: A hard instruction lands: in a hadith, a khutbah, your own conscience. You feel the urge to argue it away. {idea}Try their words instead: I hear, I obey, forgive me where I fall short.{/idea}
old: I will accept the parts of faith that feel easy.
new: I believe in all of it and answer like the Companions: we hear, we obey, forgive us.
try: Recite the last two verses of Al-Baqarah tonight before you sleep.

title: Allah never asks more than you can carry. Then ask Him.
subtitle: Every line of this dua was answered: I have done so
then: After the Companions said we hear and obey, Allah sent this verse. Muslim records that after {reward}each line of the dua, Allah said: I have done so{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says {idea}passing thoughts one cannot control are not punished{/idea}, and disliking evil thoughts is itself part of faith. The Prophet ﷺ said: I was sent with the easy, upright way.
now: The exam you failed despite studying. The prayer you forgot. The burden that feels too heavy at 2am. {reward}Allah knows your limit better than you do, and He set it.{/reward} The surah ends by putting this dua in your mouth.
old: I am being crushed by more than I can handle.
new: Allah does not burden me beyond my capacity, and He has promised to answer this dua.
try: Memorize the final dua of Al-Baqarah, one line a day, starting with Rabbana la tu'akhidhna.
